title: You 2.0: Regrets, I Have a Few...

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: Whether or not you believe in them, you probably have ghosts that haunt you.
sentences.zh: 无论你是否相信鬼魂，你可能都有挥之不去的“心魔”。

sentences.en: Not something sinister, but something you just can't get rid of.
sentences.zh: 那不是什么邪恶的东西，而是你无法摆脱的某种念头。

sentences.en: These ghosts are relentless, and they will make you rehash details from your past over and over again.
sentences.zh: 这些心魔纠缠不休，会让你一遍又一遍地反刍过去的细节。

sentences.en: Hello, Shankar.
sentences.zh: 你好，尚卡尔。

sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: I was calling about...
sentences.zh: 我打电话是想说……

sentences.en: Blue Eyes saying it.
sentences.zh: 蓝眼睛说的话。

sentences.en: Regrets have had a few, so I won't list all of them.
sentences.zh: 遗憾我有过一些，所以我就不一一列举了。

sentences.en: My boyfriend of a year and I ended our relationship.
sentences.zh: 我和交往了一年的男友分手了。

sentences.en: It's just looking back and thinking that I could have done better, and I didn't.
sentences.zh: 回首往事，我总觉得当时本可以做得更好，但我没有。

sentences.en: All these things keep popping in my head of small things, maybe something I should have said differently
sentences.zh: 脑海里总是不断浮现出一些琐事，比如在某次对话中，我本该换种说法，

sentences.en: or something I should have done differently in a particular conversation or on a particular event.
sentences.zh: 或者在某个特定事件中，我本该采取不同的做法。

sentences.en: It makes me cringe with regret and shame.
sentences.zh: 这让我因懊悔和羞愧而感到难受。

sentences.en: I had an affair.
sentences.zh: 我曾有过一段婚外情。

sentences.en: Everyone knows that it's not a secret, but it's a regret.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道，这不是什么秘密，但确实是我的遗憾。

sentences.en: My great regret is leaving Woodstock on Saturday morning.
sentences.zh: 我最大的遗憾是周六早上离开了伍德斯托克音乐节。

sentences.en: I was an evangelical Christian at the time, and I remember my friends asking me if I thought they were going to hell.
sentences.zh: 那时我是一名福音派基督徒，我记得朋友们问我，是否认为他们会下地狱。

sentences.en: And I told them that I thought they would go to hell if they did not become Christian.
sentences.zh: 我告诉他们，如果他们不皈依基督教，我想他们会下地狱。

sentences.en: And it's something that's bothered me for the last 10 years.
sentences.zh: 这件事困扰了我整整十年。

sentences.en: I am experiencing regrets on sometimes a minute-by-minute basis.
sentences.zh: 我有时甚至每分钟都在经历懊悔。

sentences.en: And it is the biggest regret of my life, honestly.
sentences.zh: 老实说，这是我一生中最大的遗憾。

sentences.en: That's it.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: I hope you have a great rest of your day.
sentences.zh: 祝你余下的一天过得愉快。

sentences.en: Bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。

sentences.en: Today on Hidden Brain, we're going to conclude our annual U2.0 series with a look at regrets.
sentences.zh: 今天的《隐藏的大脑》，我们将通过审视“遗憾”来结束我们的年度“U2.0”系列节目。

sentences.en: Why our tendency to dwell on the past may actually be helping us to prepare for the future.
sentences.zh: 为什么我们沉溺于过去的倾向，实际上可能有助于我们为未来做准备？

sentences.en: Amy Somerville is a senior research scientist at Kairos Research.
sentences.zh: 艾米·萨默维尔是凯罗斯研究中心的高级研究科学家。

sentences.en: When we spoke with her, she was a psychology professor running the Regret Lab at Miami University of Ohio.
sentences.zh: 我们采访她时，她还是俄亥俄州迈阿密大学的心理学教授，负责运营“遗憾实验室”。

sentences.en: I don't know that I have a particular deep backstory about how I got into regret.
sentences.zh: 我不知道自己是否有什么特别深刻的背景故事，解释我是如何开始研究遗憾的。

sentences.en: I actually was just generally interested in social psychology.
sentences.zh: 我其实只是对社会心理学普遍感兴趣。

sentences.en: And one of the things that then drew me to regret from that is the fact that regret is among our most common emotions.
sentences.zh: 而让我从社会心理学转向研究遗憾的原因之一，是遗憾是我们最常见的情绪之一。

sentences.en: By some estimates, it's the second most common emotion mentioned in daily life and the most common negative emotion that we mention.
sentences.zh: 据估计，它是日常生活中被提及次数第二多的情绪，也是我们提到的最常见的负面情绪。

sentences.en: And so this is really a pervasive part of how people experience the world around them.
sentences.zh: 所以，这确实是人们体验周围世界时无处不在的一部分。

sentences.en: And as I learned more, I really started to realize that regret is actually a very hopeful emotion.
sentences.zh: 随着深入了解，我开始意识到，遗憾实际上是一种非常有希望的情绪。

sentences.en: It's something that is helping us learn from our mistakes and do better in the future.
sentences.zh: 它能帮助我们从错误中学习，并在未来做得更好。

sentences.en: So it's actually, I think, a really positive thing to get to study.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，能研究这个课题其实是一件非常积极的事情。

sentences.en: Amy, I'd like to structure this conversation around a couple of stories of regret.
sentences.zh: 艾米，我想围绕几个关于遗憾的故事来展开这次对话。

sentences.en: We actually reached out to listeners of Hidden Brain some time ago, and they sent in stories about some of the things they regret in life.
sentences.zh: 我们前段时间联系了《隐藏的大脑》的听众，他们发来了自己人生中一些遗憾的故事。

sentences.en: One came from Tom Bonsaint of Arlington, Virginia.
sentences.zh: 其中一个来自弗吉尼亚州阿灵顿的汤姆·邦圣特。

sentences.en: Here's the tip.
sentences.zh: 这是他的经历。

sentences.en: I'm one of a big deal, considering that freshmen typically don't get those sort of roles.
sentences.zh: 我当时还是个大一新生，能得到那种角色非常了不起，因为新生通常拿不到那样的角色。

sentences.en: And rather than accept the fact that the director felt like I would be a good choice for the role,
sentences.zh: 但导演觉得我是个好人选，我却没有接受这个事实，

sentences.en: I listened to people who said that I probably couldn't handle it and therefore decided to turn the role down.
sentences.zh: 反而听信了别人说我可能胜任不了的话，于是决定拒绝这个角色。

sentences.en: Later on in life, I realized that when people present me with an opportunity for me being able to be successful,
sentences.zh: 后来我意识到，当人们给我提供成功的机会时，

sentences.en: they're likely not putting me in that place to put my hand up and say yes.
sentences.zh: 他们很可能并不是为了让我去推辞，而是希望我能挺身而出说“我愿意”。

sentences.en: I'm wondering how common this is.
sentences.zh: 我想知道这种情况有多普遍。

sentences.en: Are people really good at taking what happened in the past and learning from it?
sentences.zh: 人们真的擅长从过去发生的事情中吸取教训吗？

sentences.en: What spells the difference between people who actually are behaving like Tom,
sentences.zh: 是什么造成了差异？有些人像汤姆一样，

sentences.en: taking a bad experience and saying, I'm actually going to use it,
sentences.zh: 把糟糕的经历当作垫脚石，说“我要利用它”，

sentences.en: and people who just sort of stay stuck in what that bad experience was and think about it over and over again?
sentences.zh: 而另一些人却沉溺于那段糟糕的经历，反复纠结？

sentences.en: So I think the thing that really characterizes it is less about necessarily what kind of person you are,
sentences.zh: 我认为，真正区分这两者的，与其说取决于你是哪种人，

sentences.en: but rather the way that you're experiencing these thoughts.
sentences.zh: 不如说取决于你体验这些想法的方式。

sentences.en: So there's something called rumination, which actually comes literally from bovine digestion,
sentences.zh: 有一种现象叫“反刍”，这个词字面上源于牛的消化过程，

sentences.en: the idea of how cows vomit back up things, chew them over, swallow them back down, and so on and so forth.
sentences.zh: 也就是牛把吃下去的东西吐出来，重新咀嚼，再咽下去，如此反复。

sentences.en: And in terms of our thoughts, it's actually this idea of the same kind of process,
sentences.zh: 就我们的思维而言，其实也是同样的过程，

sentences.en: that rumination is having thoughts sort of spring unwanted to mind,
sentences.zh: 反刍是指那些不请自来的想法不断涌现，

sentences.en: and we're chewing them over without actually getting anything new out of them.
sentences.zh: 而我们却在反复咀嚼它们，却没能从中获得任何新的东西。

sentences.en: They're just repeatedly, intrusively becoming sort of part of our mental landscape.
sentences.zh: 它们只是反复地、侵入性地成为了我们心理图景的一部分。

sentences.en: And what we've found is that people who have ruminative regrets,
sentences.zh: 我们发现，那些有“反刍式遗憾”的人，

sentences.en: so that they're both having this regret but also having it be something that's intrusive and repeated,
sentences.zh: 也就是说，他们不仅有遗憾，而且这种遗憾是侵入性的、反复出现的，

sentences.en: tend to be people who are also experiencing the most negative outcomes,
sentences.zh: 往往也是那些经历最负面后果的人，

sentences.en: so are more likely to have clinical depression symptoms, anxiety symptoms, things like that.
sentences.zh: 所以他们更有可能出现临床抑郁症状、焦虑症状等等。

sentences.en: There are some regrets you can learn from, like Tom's story about trying out for the school play,
sentences.zh: 有些遗憾是可以从中学习的，比如汤姆试镜学校剧目的故事，

sentences.en: but other regrets feel harder to overcome.
sentences.zh: 但其他遗憾则感觉更难克服。

sentences.en: I asked Amy Somerville about this, and I played her the story from Catherine Wigginton Green,
sentences.zh: 我问了艾米·萨默维尔关于这一点，并给她播放了凯瑟琳·威金顿·格林的故事，

sentences.en: a listener from Washington, D.C.
sentences.zh: 她是来自华盛顿特区的一位听众。

sentences.en: My main regret, what popped into my mind when I heard this on the podcast,
sentences.zh: 我主要的遗憾，也就是我在播客里听到这个话题时脑海中浮现的，

sentences.en: was regretting not stopping and seeing my estranged father.
sentences.zh: 是遗憾当时没有停下车去见我疏远的父亲。

sentences.en: He'd been estranged from our family for quite a while,
sentences.zh: 他与我们家疏远了很长一段时间，

sentences.en: and I had not seen him or spoken with him in a very long time, his choice.
sentences.zh: 我很久没有见过他，也没有和他说过话，这是他的选择。

sentences.en: And I was driving along Rock Creek Parkway with my boyfriend at the time, who is now my husband.
sentences.zh: 当时我正和当时的男友（也就是现在的丈夫）开车经过岩溪公园大道。

sentences.en: And as we were driving up Rock Creek Parkway,
sentences.zh: 当我们沿着岩溪公园大道行驶时，

sentences.en: I looked to my right and saw him and the woman he married walking arm in arm.
sentences.zh: 我向右看，看到他和他的妻子手挽手走着。

sentences.en: And I saw him, and I told my husband to pull over immediately without thinking.
sentences.zh: 我看到了他，没多想就告诉丈夫立刻靠边停车。

sentences.en: And when we stopped the car, I started to unbuckle my seatbelt.
sentences.zh: 车停下后，我开始解开安全带。

sentences.en: And then I stopped and paused for a moment and realized I had no idea what I was going to do
sentences.zh: 然后我停顿了一下，意识到我根本不知道自己要做什么，

sentences.en: or what I was going to say.
sentences.zh: 也不知道该说什么。

sentences.en: So I chickened out and buckled my seatbelt back and told my husband to keep driving.
sentences.zh: 所以我退缩了，重新系好安全带，让丈夫继续开车。

sentences.en: And then I burst into tears.
sentences.zh: 然后我泪如雨下。

sentences.en: And I realized that that was probably the last time I was going to see him,
sentences.zh: 我意识到那可能是我最后一次见到他，

sentences.en: and that was my only chance to talk to him again.
sentences.zh: 那是我再次与他交谈的唯一机会。

sentences.en: So I still regret that.
sentences.zh: 所以我至今仍为此感到遗憾。

sentences.en: There's something really poignant about that story, Amy,
sentences.zh: 艾米，那个故事真的很令人心酸，

sentences.en: because in this case, it doesn't sound as if the regret has the potential for learning.
sentences.zh: 因为在这种情况下，听起来这个遗憾并没有学习的可能性。

sentences.en: She says that she feels that the door was closed in terms of her ability to reconnect with her father.
sentences.zh: 她说她觉得与父亲重新建立联系的大门已经关闭了。

sentences.en: And she comes back to this memory over and over again
sentences.zh: 她一遍又一遍地回想起这段记忆，

sentences.en: and just remembers it as an opportunity that was loSt.
sentences.zh: 只把它当作一个错失的机会。

sentences.en: Yeah, certainly in terms of the specific incidents that we regret,
sentences.zh: 是的，当然，就我们遗憾的具体事件而言，

sentences.en: they do seem to be most likely things where we had this opportunity in the moment,
sentences.zh: 它们确实最可能是那些我们在当下有机会，

sentences.en: but it's not something that we can go back and fix.
sentences.zh: 但事后却无法回头去修复的事情。

sentences.en: Because obviously, if we could just magically turn back and fix something,
sentences.zh: 因为很显然，如果我们能像变魔术一样回头修复某件事，

sentences.en: then most people would do that rather than continue to regret it.
sentences.zh: 那么大多数人都会那样做，而不是继续为此感到遗憾。

sentences.en: What I might say is that I would imagine that one of the reasons that this does rankle for this woman
sentences.zh: 我想说的是，我可以想象，这个女人之所以对此耿耿于怀，

sentences.en: is that it's about something that's important to her.
sentences.zh: 是因为这件事对她来说很重要。

sentences.en: It's about her family and that perhaps this is something that she can carry forward
sentences.zh: 这关乎她的家庭，也许这可以成为她未来处理其他人际关系时，

sentences.en: in terms of how she handles other relationships going forward.
sentences.zh: 可以借鉴的经验。

sentences.en: So I've heard people say that there are anecdotal reports
sentences.zh: 我听人说过，有一些轶事报告称，

sentences.en: that the things that people really regret are the things that they didn't do
sentences.zh: 人们真正遗憾的事情，往往是他们“没有做”的事，

sentences.en: rather than the things that they did do.
sentences.zh: 而不是他们“做过”的事。

sentences.en: Is that just anecdotal?
sentences.zh: 这只是轶事吗？

sentences.en: Is that not actually true that people regret acts of omission more than acts of commission?
sentences.zh: 人们对“不作为”的遗憾真的比对“作为”的遗憾更多吗？

sentences.en: I would say there's some evidence for that.
sentences.zh: 我想是有一些证据支持这一点的。

sentences.en: So one of the more famous studies on this thought about this in terms of something that happens over time.
sentences.zh: 关于这一点，一项比较著名的研究从时间推移的角度进行了思考。

sentences.en: And what those researchers argued is that we regret things we did a lot more in the moment.
sentences.zh: 那些研究人员认为，在当下，我们对做过的事情感到遗憾要多得多。

sentences.en: So if you say something really stupid in a job interview,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你在面试中说了非常愚蠢的话，

sentences.en: you're going to walk out and have that hand to the forehead feeling of,
sentences.zh: 你走出来时会有一种拍着额头的感觉，

sentences.en: oh, why did I say that?
sentences.zh: “噢，我为什么要那样说？”

sentences.en: That was such a terrible thing to have said in that moment.
sentences.zh: 在那一刻，那真是太糟糕了。

sentences.en: But in the long run, we tend to have things that are kind of incomplete goals stick around in our memory
sentences.zh: 但从长远来看，我们往往会把那些未完成的目标留在记忆中，

sentences.en: as kind of a mental to-do list, basically.
sentences.zh: 基本上就像一份心理待办事项清单。

sentences.en: And that as a result, our inactions wind up getting kind of added to that mental to-do liSt.
sentences.zh: 结果就是，我们的不作为最终会被添加到那份心理待办事项清单中。

sentences.en: So this may be something where if you ask me, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以这可能就是，如果你问我，你知道，

sentences.en: what could you have done instead of going to grad school?
sentences.zh: “如果不去读研，你还能做什么？”

sentences.en: I have this whole range of possibilities.
sentences.zh: 我有各种各样的可能性。

sentences.en: I could have been a doctor.
sentences.zh: 我可以成为一名医生。

sentences.en: I could have been a writer.
sentences.zh: 我可以成为一名作家。

sentences.en: I could have backpacked around Europe and found my passion.
sentences.zh: 我可以背着背包环游欧洲，找到我的热情所在。

sentences.en: And if you ask me, what are the things that you did yesterday that you could undo?
sentences.zh: 而如果你问我，昨天做的哪些事是可以撤销的？

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对吧。

sentences.en: I have a finite set of things I actually did in my life.
sentences.zh: 我一生中实际做过的事情是有限的。

sentences.en: And so over time, it may be that when we're trying to undo something bad that's happened to us,
sentences.zh: 所以随着时间的推移，当我们试图撤销发生在我们身上的坏事时，

sentences.en: it's easy to start imagining all of the things we might have done in the past
sentences.zh: 我们很容易开始想象过去所有可能做过的事情，

sentences.en: because we have a lot more of those available to us than the things we actually did.
sentences.zh: 因为相比于我们实际做过的事情，我们有更多这类想象空间。

sentences.en: There are times when we don't take responsibility for our actions.
sentences.zh: 有时我们不对自己的行为负责。

sentences.en: But at other times, we hold ourselves accountable for things that are outside our control.
sentences.zh: 但有时，我们又会为那些超出我们控制范围的事情承担责任。

sentences.en: James Cooper of Pittsburgh shared one of those stories with us.
sentences.zh: 匹兹堡的詹姆斯·库珀与我们分享了其中一个故事。

sentences.en: My biggest regret is not listening to my father tell me about the mundane things that happened to him during the day
sentences.zh: 我最大的遗憾是，当父亲打电话给我，想告诉我他白天发生的琐事时，我没有听，

sentences.en: and instead just immediately asking for my mom when I called the house.
sentences.zh: 而是直接问我妈在哪。

sentences.en: Maybe when I talked to him, I could have picked up on some other signs too
sentences.zh: 也许如果我当时和他多聊聊，我能察觉到其他一些迹象，

sentences.en: and could have maybe prevented his suicide.
sentences.zh: 也许就能阻止他自杀。

sentences.en: You know, when I heard James' story, Amy, I wondered whether, you know, if he had spoken to his father more,
sentences.zh: 你知道，艾米，当我听到詹姆斯的故事时，我心想，如果他当时多和父亲说说话，

sentences.en: would he have actually picked up on his father's mental health?
sentences.zh: 他真的能察觉到父亲的心理健康问题吗？

sentences.en: And even if he had noticed, could he have actually stopped his father from committing suicide?
sentences.zh: 即使他注意到了，他真的能阻止父亲自杀吗？

sentences.en: And it seemed to me that in this case, James might have been taking on more responsibility than was actually warranted.
sentences.zh: 在我看来，在这种情况下，詹姆斯可能承担了超出实际需要的责任。

sentences.en: I mean, it's understandable, certainly at an emotional level.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在情感层面上，这当然是可以理解的。

sentences.en: But you've done some research looking at how sometimes when it comes to regret,
sentences.zh: 但你做过一些研究，观察到有时在遗憾这件事上，

sentences.en: we take on more responsibility than we should.
sentences.zh: 我们承担了比我们应该承担的更多的责任。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think I would say exactly that.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想我完全同意这一点。

sentences.en: I think that this is a case of probably imagining that there's more that could have happened differently.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是一个典型的例子，人们往往会想象有更多的事情本可以以不同的方式发生。

sentences.en: And it's certainly the case as well that I think people often tend to focus a lot on their own actions about negative events.
sentences.zh: 而且确实，我认为人们往往倾向于在负面事件中过多地关注自己的行为。

sentences.en: And it's probably important to think about the fact that you're just one agent in a much bigger framework,
sentences.zh: 思考这样一个事实可能很重要：你只是一个更大框架中的一个参与者，

sentences.en: that his father had other friends, hopefully had doctors, had his mother,
sentences.zh: 他的父亲还有其他朋友，希望还有医生，还有他的母亲，

sentences.en: and that it's not just on James to have recognized these symptoms,
sentences.zh: 所以识别这些症状不仅仅是詹姆斯的责任，

sentences.en: but that there were lots of other pieces that could have played out differently,
sentences.zh: 还有很多其他因素本可以有不同的走向，

sentences.en: not just his own actions, but a broader set of things that could have changed.
sentences.zh: 不仅仅是他自己的行为，而是一系列更广泛的事情本可以改变。

sentences.en: Is there a way for people to look at their regrets and say,
sentences.zh: 人们有没有办法审视自己的遗憾，然后说，

sentences.en: this is the kind of regret that is actually useful and productive,
sentences.zh: “这是一种实际上有用且富有成效的遗憾”？

sentences.en: and this is the kind of regret that is actually better set aside?
sentences.zh: 那么，这种遗憾是否其实最好还是放下呢？

sentences.en: So I would say that we know that people tend to generate these what-if thoughts
sentences.zh: 我会说，我们知道人们倾向于产生这些“如果……会怎样”的想法，

sentences.en: as a way of trying to understand their experiences
sentences.zh: 以此作为试图理解自身经历的一种方式，

sentences.en: and as a way of trying to bring control to things that feel uncontrollable.
sentences.zh: 也作为一种试图掌控那些感觉无法掌控之事的方式。

sentences.en: We don't like the idea that bad things happen with no reason and without the ability to predict them.
sentences.zh: 我们不喜欢坏事无缘无故发生且无法预测的想法。

sentences.en: And in the case of regret, I think it can be that in James's case, for instance,
sentences.zh: 就遗憾而言，我认为在詹姆斯（James）的例子中，

sentences.en: not wanting to think about this tremendous loss as something that wasn't predictable
sentences.zh: 不想把这种巨大的损失看作是无法预测、

sentences.en: and wasn't controllable, that it's, I think, very reassuring sometimes
sentences.zh: 无法掌控的事情，我认为，有时能试图找出一个解释，

sentences.en: to try to come up with an explanation of there's a way that this could have been prevented,
sentences.zh: 即这件事本可以被预防、

sentences.en: it could have been changed, and it feels less random and less senseless in that way.
sentences.zh: 本可以被改变，这会让人感到非常安心，这样一来，事情感觉就不那么随机、不那么毫无意义了。

sentences.en: You know, I'm fascinated by what you just said, because essentially what you're saying is that
sentences.zh: 你知道，你刚才说的话让我很着迷，因为你本质上是在说，

sentences.en: the fear or the pain of having a world that seems, you know, without meaning
sentences.zh: 那种面对一个似乎毫无意义、

sentences.en: or is unexplainable or unpredictable, that pain of that might actually be greater
sentences.zh: 无法解释或不可预测的世界的恐惧或痛苦，这种痛苦实际上可能比

sentences.en: than the pain of taking on regrets for things that you actually maybe don't have responsibility for
sentences.zh: 为那些你可能并不负责的事情承担遗憾，

sentences.en: and experiencing personal anguish about it.
sentences.zh: 并因此经历个人痛苦的痛苦还要大。

sentences.en: That's a fascinating idea.
sentences.zh: 这是一个引人入胜的观点。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: There's been research that says one of the ways that people can get a sense of control over their
sentences.zh: 有研究表明，人们获得对自身环境掌控感的方式之一，

sentences.en: circumstances is by having these thoughts about what might have been.
sentences.zh: 就是产生这些关于“如果当初怎样”的想法。

sentences.en: The dark side of that, along with personal regret, is there is also work where things like victim
sentences.zh: 其阴暗面在于，除了个人遗憾，还有研究表明，像受害者

sentences.en: blaming can actually come out of these thoughts about what might have been.
sentences.zh: 指责这样的事情，实际上也可能源于这些关于“如果当初怎样”的想法。

sentences.en: So if you think about a woman who attended a party and drank a drink that had been drugged
sentences.zh: 所以，如果你想到一个去参加聚会并喝了一杯被下药的饮料，

sentences.en: and then was sexually assaulted, right, it's very easy to think about that one moment of
sentences.zh: 然后遭到性侵的女性，对吧，很容易想到那一刻，

sentences.en: she took this drink.
sentences.zh: 她喝了那杯饮料。

sentences.en: And if she had been more careful, then this assault might not have happened to her.
sentences.zh: 如果她当时更小心一点，那么这次侵犯可能就不会发生在她身上。

sentences.en: And that that sort of gives us a sense of control rather than the much more complicated thing to
sentences.zh: 这给了我们一种掌控感，而不是去思考更复杂的事情，

sentences.en: think about undoing of, well, how could we have prevented this person who gave her this
sentences.zh: 比如，我们该如何阻止那个给她下药、

sentences.en: drink and who committed this crime from doing it?
sentences.zh: 犯下这起罪行的人呢？

sentences.en: So, yeah, these thoughts about what might have been helped give us a causal structure to our
sentences.zh: 所以，是的，这些关于“如果当初怎样”的想法，有助于为我们的

sentences.en: world.
sentences.zh: 世界提供一种因果结构。

sentences.en: But sometimes they're not necessarily the correct or the most useful ways of thinking about
sentences.zh: 但有时它们并不一定是正确或最有用的思考

sentences.en: causality.
sentences.zh: 因果关系的方式。

sentences.en: When we come back, a story of regret and karma.
sentences.zh: 稍后回来，我们将讲述一个关于遗憾与因果报应的故事。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》（Hidden Brain）。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆（Shankar Vedantam）。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: I'm back with Amy Somerville.
sentences.zh: 我与艾米·萨默维尔（Amy Somerville）一起回来继续探讨。

sentences.en: Amy, let's listen to another story.
sentences.zh: 艾米，让我们听听另一个故事。

sentences.en: This one comes from Tanya Stark of Farmington, New Mexico.
sentences.zh: 这个故事来自新墨西哥州法明顿的坦尼娅·斯塔克（Tanya Stark）。

sentences.en: I'm going to play the story in two parts because I think it reveals two different sides of regret.
sentences.zh: 我打算分两部分播放这个故事，因为我认为它揭示了遗憾的两个不同侧面。

sentences.en: One of my biggest regrets comes from something I did in the fifth grade 20 or more years ago.
sentences.zh: 我最大的遗憾之一源于我小学五年级时做的一件事，那已经是20多年前的事了。

sentences.en: I remember making fun of this little girl who was a bit overweight and me and another girl
sentences.zh: 我记得当时嘲笑了一个有点超重的小女孩，我和另一个女孩

sentences.en: just teased her relentlessly and I think about some of the things that I said to her and some of the ways
sentences.zh: 不停地戏弄她，我想到我当时对她说的一些话，以及我对待她的

sentences.en: that I treated her and I just regret how cruel I was as a child.
sentences.zh: 一些方式，我真的很后悔自己小时候是那么残忍。

sentences.en: And now that I'm older and I work in a field where I see the effects of what bullying and meanness
sentences.zh: 现在我长大了，从事的领域让我看到了霸凌和刻薄

sentences.en: does to children, I am so full of regret in that and if I could ever find her again or talk to her again
sentences.zh: 对孩子造成的伤害，我对此充满了遗憾。如果我能再次找到她或与她交谈，

sentences.en: because I've moved to three or four different places at this point in my life and have no idea where she is
sentences.zh: 因为我这辈子已经搬了三四次家，根本不知道她在哪里，

sentences.en: or if it even affected her, I regret the way that I treated her and I believe that I was so cruel.
sentences.zh: 或者那件事是否真的影响了她，我为我对待她的方式感到后悔，我相信我当时太残忍了。

sentences.en: Amy, I want to talk about the role of guilt and regret.
sentences.zh: 艾米，我想谈谈内疚和遗憾的作用。

sentences.en: They seem closely tied, these two emotions, but I don't think they're identical.
sentences.zh: 这两种情绪似乎紧密相连，但我不认为它们是完全相同的。

sentences.en: Tom Bonsaint from Arlington, Virginia, regretted that he didn't get the lead in his school play,
sentences.zh: 来自弗吉尼亚州阿灵顿的汤姆·邦圣（Tom Bonsaint）很遗憾自己没有在学校的戏剧中担任主角，

sentences.en: but there was no guilt involved.
sentences.zh: 但这其中并不涉及内疚。

sentences.en: Tanya, on the other hand, feels terrible about what she did.
sentences.zh: 而坦尼娅则对自己的所作所为感到非常糟糕。

sentences.en: When you hear Tanya's story, are you hearing guilt or are you hearing regret?
sentences.zh: 当你听到坦尼娅的故事时，你听到的是内疚还是遗憾？

sentences.en: So listening to Tanya's story, I would say I hear both guilt and regret.
sentences.zh: 听了坦尼娅的故事，我会说我既听到了内疚，也听到了遗憾。

sentences.en: And both regret and guilt are emotions that are based on a form of comparison.
sentences.zh: 遗憾和内疚都是基于某种比较的情绪。

sentences.en: So regret, I'm comparing what really happened to some imagined alternative.
sentences.zh: 遗憾是，我将现实发生的事情与某种想象中的替代方案进行比较。

sentences.en: And some of the time, that's all we feel, right?
sentences.zh: 有时，我们感受到的仅仅是这些，对吧？

sentences.en: I just imagine that something could have been better.
sentences.zh: 我只是想象事情本可以更好。

sentences.en: Guilt involves an additional comparison to what has been called our personal standards, rules, and goals.
sentences.zh: 内疚则涉及与所谓的个人标准、规则和目标的额外比较。

sentences.en: So what are the things that we aspire to in our behavior?
sentences.zh: 那么，我们在行为上追求的是什么呢？

sentences.en: And when we make a comparison that says what we really did falls short of those personal standards, rules, or goals for ourselves,
sentences.zh: 当我们进行比较，发现我们的实际行为未能达到那些个人标准、规则或目标时，

sentences.en: then we're likely to feel guilt.
sentences.zh: 我们很可能会感到内疚。

sentences.en: I want you to listen to the second part of Tanya's story.
sentences.zh: 我想请你听听坦尼娅故事的第二部分。

sentences.en: She told us that she fully realized what she had done to this other little kid,
sentences.zh: 她告诉我们，她完全意识到自己对那个小孩子做了什么，

sentences.en: only when events in her own life took a turn.
sentences.zh: 是在她自己的人生发生转折之后。

sentences.en: I think karma came and got me because while I was a petite little kid,
sentences.zh: 我想是因果报应找上我了，因为虽然我小时候是个娇小的孩子，

sentences.en: as I got older and through some injuries, I became quite overweight myself
sentences.zh: 但随着年龄增长，经历了一些伤病，我自己也变得相当超重，

sentences.en: and heard the comments that were said about me or how I became invisible.
sentences.zh: 也听到了别人对我的评价，或者感受到了自己是如何变得“隐形”的。

sentences.en: And people didn't think that my feelings mattered.
sentences.zh: 人们认为我的感受并不重要。

sentences.en: The heaviest I ever was was 330 pounds.
sentences.zh: 我最重的时候达到了330磅。

sentences.en: And I have worked hard and had surgery and have lost quite a bit of weight.
sentences.zh: 我努力工作，做了手术，减掉了不少体重。

sentences.en: I'm just about 195 now, but I still see myself and still have the self-confidence of a 330-pound woman.
sentences.zh: 我现在大约195磅，但我依然用330磅时的眼光看自己，依然有着那时女性的自卑感。

sentences.en: And I know how it feels, and I regret making anyone else ever feel that way.
sentences.zh: 我知道那种感觉，我很后悔曾让任何人有过那种感受。

sentences.en: When you listen to Tanya's story, Amy, I'm wondering, do you hear sort of someone saying,
sentences.zh: 艾米，当你听坦尼娅的故事时，我在想，你听到的是有人在说：

sentences.en: I really don't like the way the world has treated me?
sentences.zh: “我真的很不喜欢这个世界对待我的方式”吗？

sentences.en: Or do you hear someone saying, I realize the world has treated me really badly,
sentences.zh: 还是你听到的是有人在说：“我意识到世界对待我真的很糟糕，

sentences.en: and that's opened my eyes to the way that I might have treated other people in the past?
sentences.zh: 这让我看清了过去我可能对待别人的方式”？

sentences.en: It sounds like in Tanya's case, she's really developed a different understanding of the world
sentences.zh: 听起来在坦尼娅的案例中，她确实对世界有了不同的理解，

sentences.en: and used that to understand how her behavior may have affected other people
sentences.zh: 并利用这种理解去认识她的行为可能如何影响了他人，

sentences.en: rather than necessarily being particularly focused on feeling that she's been treated badly.
sentences.zh: 而不是仅仅专注于觉得自己受到了不公正的对待。

sentences.en: And I think that, again, regret is based on this idea that we personally could have done something differently.
sentences.zh: 我认为，遗憾再次基于这样一种观念：我们个人本可以采取不同的做法。

sentences.en: And so in some ways, it's obviously a self-focused emotion.
sentences.zh: 所以从某种程度上说，这显然是一种以自我为中心的情绪。

sentences.en: It's about what we should have done.
sentences.zh: 它关乎我们本该做什么。

sentences.en: But I think it can also be a fairly selfless emotion
sentences.zh: 但我认为它也可以是一种相当无私的情绪，

sentences.en: and be about how we relate to the people in the world around us.
sentences.zh: 关乎我们如何与周围的人建立联系。

sentences.en: What responsibility do we have towards our fellow humans?
sentences.zh: 我们对同胞负有什么责任？

sentences.en: One of the things that I really hear Tanya talking about is,
sentences.zh: 坦尼娅所谈论的内容中，我真正听到的一点是：

sentences.en: I wish that I could find this person and tell her about how I now regret what I did to her when we were children.
sentences.zh: 我希望我能找到那个人，告诉她我现在有多后悔小时候对她做过的事。

sentences.en: And I think one of the things as well that's interesting about this whole episode
sentences.zh: 我认为关于这一整集节目，还有一点很有趣，

sentences.en: is that you have listeners calling in to tell the whole world,
sentences.zh: 那就是有听众打电话来告诉全世界，

sentences.en: millions of people who might listen to this podcast,
sentences.zh: 数百万可能收听这个播客的人，

sentences.en: about their very personal, very private regrets.
sentences.zh: 关于他们非常个人、非常私密的遗憾。

sentences.en: You know, psychologists have talked for a long time about something called the fundamental attribution error,
sentences.zh: 你知道，心理学家长期以来一直在谈论一种叫做“基本归因错误”的东西，

sentences.en: which is how much do we believe actions of either ourselves or others are caused by things that are intrinsic to us,
sentences.zh: 即我们有多相信自己或他人的行为是由我们内在的东西引起的，

sentences.en: things that are part of who our personalities, who we are, versus things that are shaped by the context,
sentences.zh: 那些是我们性格的一部分、是我们本身的东西，而不是由环境塑造的，

sentences.en: by the situation in which we find ourselves.
sentences.zh: 由我们所处的具体情境所塑造的。

sentences.en: When someone like Tanya looks back as an adult at her behavior as a child,
sentences.zh: 当像坦尼娅这样的人作为成年人回顾她小时候的行为时，

sentences.en: do you think the fundamental attribution error plays a role in some ways leading us to believe
sentences.zh: 你认为基本归因错误在某种程度上是否导致我们相信，

sentences.en: that we are responsible for things that maybe we were not responsible for,
sentences.zh: 我们对那些可能并非我们负责的事情负有责任，

sentences.en: that maybe really the context was driving our actions and behavior way back when?
sentences.zh: 也许当时真的是环境在驱动我们的行为？

sentences.en: Yeah, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 是的，绝对是这样。

sentences.en: Again, I think regret is based on this sense of personal responsibility.
sentences.zh: 再说一次，我认为遗憾是基于这种个人责任感。

sentences.en: And certainly in Western cultures, there's very much this belief that, you know,
sentences.zh: 当然，在西方文化中，人们非常相信，你知道，

sentences.en: individuals are responsible for their own actions, we're responsible for our own destinies.
sentences.zh: 个人要为自己的行为负责，我们要为自己的命运负责。

sentences.en: And I think that can lead individuals to think more about how a given actor,
sentences.zh: 我认为这会导致个人更多地思考某个行为主体，

sentences.en: including themselves or including another person, played a role,
sentences.zh: 包括他们自己或他人，是如何发挥作用的，

sentences.en: and a lot less attention to the whole context.
sentences.zh: 而对整个环境的关注则少得多。

sentences.en: So in Tanya's story, I believe she started by talking about how there was another little girl
sentences.zh: 所以在坦尼娅的故事中，我相信她开头提到，有另一个小女孩

sentences.en: that she was friends with who joined with her in the bullying.
sentences.zh: 是她的朋友，也加入了霸凌的行列。

sentences.en: And I think it may be easy to ignore the degree to which she was experiencing peer pressure.
sentences.zh: 我认为，忽视她所经历的同伴压力程度可能很容易，

sentences.en: Right?
sentences.zh: 对吧？

sentences.en: There was probably a social context in which this bullying occurred,
sentences.zh: 这种霸凌可能发生在一个特定的社会环境中，

sentences.en: which doesn't forgive it or excuse it,
sentences.zh: 这并不能原谅或宽恕它，

sentences.en: but it's not necessarily just about who Tanya is as a person to have done this,
sentences.zh: 但这不一定仅仅关乎坦尼娅作为一个人的本质，

sentences.en: but rather really a much more complicated net of things that were influencing her
sentences.zh: 而实际上是一个更复杂的因素网，在影响着她，

sentences.en: as well as who she was at that time.
sentences.zh: 以及当时的她。

sentences.en: I want to talk about the idea of counterfactuals.
sentences.zh: 我想谈谈反事实的概念。

sentences.en: A counterfactual, of course, is when we imagine that things could have turned out differently
sentences.zh: 反事实，当然就是当我们想象事情本可以有不同的结果，

sentences.en: than they actually did.
sentences.zh: 而不是实际发生的结果时。

sentences.en: You know, as it turns out, I'm recovering right now from a sports injury.
sentences.zh: 你知道，事实证明，我目前正在从运动损伤中恢复。

sentences.en: And when I think about how I got hurt, the only thing I'm thinking about is,
sentences.zh: 当我想到我是如何受伤时，我脑子里想的唯一一件事就是：

sentences.en: what could I have done differently to prevent this injury from happening?
sentences.zh: 我本可以做些什么不同的事情来防止这次受伤发生？

sentences.en: Now, most of the time when I play sports, I'm not asking myself, why didn't I get hurt?
sentences.zh: 现在，大多数时候我进行体育运动时，我并不会问自己：为什么我没有受伤？

sentences.en: So what do you think causes us to reach for certain counterfactuals at one point in time,
sentences.zh: 那么你认为是什么导致我们在某个时间点去寻求特定的反事实，

sentences.en: but not for others?
sentences.zh: 而在其他时间点却不会呢？

sentences.en: So we talk about counterfactuals as having two different directions.
sentences.zh: 我们谈论反事实时，认为它有两个不同的方向。

sentences.en: So things imagining how the world could have been better, we call upward counterfactuals,
sentences.zh: 想象世界本可以变得更好的事情，我们称之为“上行反事实”，

sentences.en: and imagining how the world could have been worse, we call downward counterfactuals.
sentences.zh: 而想象世界本可以变得更糟的事情，我们称之为“下行反事实”。

sentences.en: And certainly in life, upward counterfactuals seem to predominate.
sentences.zh: 当然，在生活中，上行反事实似乎占主导地位。

sentences.en: And one of the reasons that we seem to do this is that these upward counterfactuals are helping us learn.
sentences.zh: 我们似乎这样做的一个原因是，这些上行反事实正在帮助我们学习。

sentences.en: So if you think about getting into a car accident, if I say, you know, if only I hadn't been texting,
sentences.zh: 所以如果你想到发生车祸，如果我说，你知道，如果我当时没有发短信，

sentences.en: then I might not have had the accident.
sentences.zh: 那么我就可能不会发生事故了。

sentences.en: That's identifying a particular cause of the accident.
sentences.zh: 那是在确定事故的一个特定原因。

sentences.en: It was the texting and not my speed or the fact that it was raining or the way that the road was engineered
sentences.zh: 是发短信，而不是我的车速，或者当时正在下雨，又或者道路工程设计

sentences.en: and designed for traffic flow.
sentences.zh: 是为了交通流量而设计的。

sentences.en: And downward counterfactuals seem to serve a different function,
sentences.zh: 而下行反事实似乎起到了不同的作用，

sentences.en: which is that they make us feel better about the things that might have happened.
sentences.zh: 那就是它们让我们对可能发生的事情感觉更好。

sentences.en: And so my collaborator, Soyeon Rim, and I have found that when people are focused on
sentences.zh: 所以我的合作者苏妍·林（Soyeon Rim）和我发现，当人们专注于

sentences.en: things from which they have a little bit of distance,
sentences.zh: 那些他们有一点距离感的事情时，

sentences.en: whether that's things that have happened more distantly in time
sentences.zh: 无论是时间上发生得比较久远的事情，

sentences.en: or things that have happened to other people versus to themselves,
sentences.zh: 还是发生在别人身上而不是自己身上的事情，

sentences.en: we're able to get into this mindset of thinking about what are the goals that we have
sentences.zh: 我们就能进入这种思维模式，去思考我们的目标是什么，

sentences.en: and what are the ways that we can use this negative event to self-improve.
sentences.zh: 以及我们如何利用这个负面事件来提升自我。

sentences.en: But for things that feel a little bit closer to us,
sentences.zh: 但对于那些感觉离我们近一点的事情，

sentences.en: so again, happening to us personally rather than to somebody else,
sentences.zh: 也就是再次强调，是个人身上发生的，而不是别人身上发生的，

sentences.en: those things we seem to be often somewhat more focused on feeling better about.
sentences.zh: 对于那些事情，我们似乎往往更专注于让自己感觉好受一点。

sentences.en: And so with the example of your injury, you know,
sentences.zh: 所以以你的伤势为例，你知道，

sentences.en: it may be the case that it's helpful to think about how things could have turned out much worse than they did,
sentences.zh: 思考事情本可能比实际情况糟糕得多，这可能是有帮助的。

sentences.en: that, you know, you're back at work, hopefully you didn't need a lot of medical intervention or surgery,
sentences.zh: 你知道，当你重返工作岗位时，希望你不需要进行大量的医疗干预或手术，

sentences.en: you know, and those would have been things that would have been much, much worse
sentences.zh: 你知道，那些情况本来会糟糕得多，

sentences.en: than walking away with just maybe a sprain or a strain.
sentences.zh: 远比仅仅受点扭伤或拉伤要严重。

sentences.en: So I'm reminded of that great study that Tom Gilovich did many years ago at the Barcelona Olympics,
sentences.zh: 所以我想到汤姆·吉洛维奇（Tom Gilovich）多年前在巴塞罗那奥运会上做的那项出色的研究，

sentences.en: where he took photographs of the people who were on the medal stand.
sentences.zh: 他给站在领奖台上的运动员拍了照片。

sentences.en: And he found, of course, that the silver medalists tend to make these upward counterfactuals,
sentences.zh: 他发现，不出所料，银牌得主往往会进行这种“向上反事实思维”，

sentences.en: and they tend to look a little less happy because they wish they had won gold,
sentences.zh: 他们看起来往往没那么开心，因为他们希望自己能拿到金牌，

sentences.en: whereas the bronze medalists tend to make downward counterfactuals.
sentences.zh: 而铜牌得主往往会进行“向下反事实思维”。

sentences.en: They imagine all the other people who didn't win any medals at all
sentences.zh: 他们会想到所有那些根本没拿到奖牌的人，

sentences.en: and find themselves relieved that they find themselves on the medals podium in the first place.
sentences.zh: 并为自己能站在领奖台上感到庆幸。

sentences.en: And this is fascinating because how this happens,
sentences.zh: 这非常引人入胜，因为这种心理过程，

sentences.en: how we choose to make the upward counterfactual or the downward counterfactual,
sentences.zh: 我们如何选择进行向上还是向下反事实思维，

sentences.en: this is largely happening unconsciously,
sentences.zh: 很大程度上是在无意识中发生的，

sentences.en: and yet this unconscious choice has an enormous effect on whether we feel happy afterwards.
sentences.zh: 然而这种无意识的选择对我们事后是否感到快乐有着巨大的影响。

sentences.en: Yeah, and one of the things that shapes particularly the medal example is
sentences.zh: 是的，特别是在奖牌这个例子中，决定因素之一是

sentences.en: how easy is it to imagine this alternative happening.
sentences.zh: 想象这种替代结果发生的难易程度。

sentences.en: So often for a silver medalist, it's much, much easier to imagine how close they were to getting gold,
sentences.zh: 对于银牌得主来说，想象自己离金牌有多近要容易得多，

sentences.en: whereas for a bronze medalist, the thing that's easiest to imagine is, yeah,
sentences.zh: 而对于铜牌得主来说，最容易想象的事情是，没错，

sentences.en: not being on the medal stand at all because those are things that are actually closer.
sentences.zh: 根本没能站上领奖台，因为这些情况实际上更贴近现实。

sentences.en: Another one of my favorite studies about counterfactuals is that if you think about a grade distribution
sentences.zh: 关于反事实思维，我最喜欢的另一项研究是，如果你考虑成绩分布，

sentences.en: where the cutoff to get an A is to get a 90% or above,
sentences.zh: 拿到A的门槛是90%或以上，

sentences.en: students who get an 89 in a course wind up being less satisfied than the students who got an 87.
sentences.zh: 课程得分为89分的学生，最终的满意度反而不如得了87分的学生。

sentences.en: Both of them have a B+, but the 89s, it's so easy to just imagine,
sentences.zh: 他们都拿到了B+，但对于89分的学生来说，太容易想象了：

sentences.en: how did you get just that one more point?
sentences.zh: 要是能再多得那一分该多好？

sentences.en: Whereas for the 87s, they tend to feel lucky that they wound up where they are
sentences.zh: 而对于87分的学生，他们往往会觉得自己能拿到这个分数很幸运，

sentences.en: and aren't imagining how they might have gotten the A- instead.
sentences.zh: 而不会去想自己本可能拿到A-。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: I understand you got married about a year ago,
sentences.zh: 我听说你大约在一年前结婚了，

sentences.en: and you applied some of your own research on regret when it came to choosing a wedding dress.
sentences.zh: 而且你在挑选婚纱时应用了你自己关于后悔的研究成果。

sentences.en: I did.
sentences.zh: 是的，我用了。

sentences.en: So I actually wasn't applying my own research.
sentences.zh: 其实我并没有应用我自己的研究。

sentences.en: I applied work by Sheena Younger on the phenomenon of choice overload,
sentences.zh: 我应用了希娜·恩格（Sheena Iyengar）关于“选择过载”现象的研究，

sentences.en: as well as work by Barry Schwartz and colleagues about the idea of maximizing
sentences.zh: 以及巴里·施瓦茨（Barry Schwartz）及其同事关于“最大化”

sentences.en: versus satisficing as strategies for decisions.
sentences.zh: 与“满意化”作为决策策略的研究。

sentences.en: Maximizing being the idea that you want to pick the best of all possible alternatives
sentences.zh: 最大化是指你想要在所有可能的选择中挑选出最好的那个，

sentences.en: and satisficing being the idea that you're going to pick something that meets all of your standards,
sentences.zh: 而满意化是指你打算挑选出符合你所有标准的东西，

sentences.en: but may or may not be the absolute beSt.
sentences.zh: 但它未必是绝对最好的。

sentences.en: So when I was wedding dress shopping, I went to a couple of stores.
sentences.zh: 所以当我去买婚纱时，我去了几家店。

sentences.en: I tried on five or 10 dresses at each one,
sentences.zh: 每家店我都试穿了五到十件礼服，

sentences.en: and I found a dress that I absolutely loved and was in my price range.
sentences.zh: 然后我找到了一件我非常喜欢且在预算范围内的婚纱。

sentences.en: And I realized that what the research told me was I would never be happier than I was at that moment,
sentences.zh: 我意识到研究告诉我的道理是：我永远不会比此刻更快乐了，

sentences.en: that if I kept dress shopping, I was going to wind up feeling overwhelmed.
sentences.zh: 如果我继续逛下去，最终只会感到不知所措。

sentences.en: You know, I could find a hundred different lace sheaths with a V-neck in ivory,
sentences.zh: 你知道，我可以找到一百种不同的象牙白V领蕾丝紧身裙，

sentences.en: and I would wind up feeling confused about what are the differences between these,
sentences.zh: 最后我会对它们之间的区别感到困惑，

sentences.en: and that the very act of trying to get the absolute best would mean that I could never really be sure if I'd done it.
sentences.zh: 而且这种试图追求绝对完美的行为，意味着我永远无法确定自己是否真的做到了最好。

sentences.en: Whereas if I adopted a satisficing strategy,
sentences.zh: 而如果我采取满意化策略，

sentences.en: I could be sure I'm in a dress that looks beautiful on me and is in my price range,
sentences.zh: 我可以确定我穿的这件婚纱既漂亮又在我的预算之内，

sentences.en: and I should just buy it and be done.
sentences.zh: 我应该直接买下它，然后就结束了。

sentences.en: And so that's how I chose my wedding dress.
sentences.zh: 这就是我选择婚纱的方式。

sentences.en: Amy Somerville is a senior research scientist at Kairos Research.
sentences.zh: 艾米·萨默维尔（Amy Somerville）是Kairos Research的高级研究科学家。

sentences.en: When we spoke with her, she was a psychology professor running the Regret Lab at Miami University of Ohio.
sentences.zh: 我们采访她时，她还是俄亥俄州迈阿密大学心理学教授，负责管理后悔实验室（Regret Lab）。

sentences.zh: 我是《Hidden Brain》的执行编辑。

sentences.zh: 本周我们默默无闻的英雄是全国各地NPR成员电台的项目总监们。

sentences.zh: 选择在公共广播电台播放的节目是非常困难的。

sentences.zh: 有太多不同的节目可供选择，

sentences.zh: 我们非常感谢那些决定将《Hidden Brain》带给听众的电台。

sentences.en: If you've enjoyed our U2.0 series the past few weeks,
sentences.zh: 如果你喜欢过去几周我们的“U2.0”系列节目，

sentences.en: please consider supporting our work.
sentences.zh: 请考虑支持我们的工作。

sentences.zh: 你可以访问 support.hiddenbrain.org 进行支持。

sentences.zh: 我是香卡·维丹塔姆（Shankar Vedantam）。

sentences.zh: 下周见。
